title: Restoring cortical disinhibition improves Huntington's disease phenotypes.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: I resolved the paper's only data link, the Zenodo deposit 10.5281/zenodo.20750675, four different ways (doi.org redirect, Zenodo REST application programming interface record endpoint, zenodo.org/records and /record HTML pages, DataCite application programming interface) and every one returned HTTP 404; two Zenodo keyword searches (author name, topic) returned no matching record. I then listed every supplementary object that actually exists: the PubMed Central full-text XML declares exactly three (MOESM1 .xlsx, MOESM2 .pdf, MOESM3 .pdf), and the Nature article HTML names the same three and no others. I downloaded MOESM1 (34,840 bytes) and opened it with openpyxl: one sheet, 187 rows x 9 columns, columns 'Figure Panel', 'Main Factor 1', 'Main Factor 1 (p value)', ... 'Posthoc pairwise comparisons' — it is a table of statistical test results (p-values), not data. I probed MOESM4 through MOESM14 in .xlsx/.zip/.csv on the Springer content delivery network: all 33 probes returned 403, i.e. no further files exist. Europe PMC's supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out on one attempt and was not retried.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All biological counts come from the article text and were not verifiable against files: 8 control plus 8 R6/2 mice and 107 behavioural sessions; VIP-interneuron imaging of 809 neurons/33 sessions/10 mice (control) and 464/38/11 (R6/2); 12 mice used for the optogenetics figures; optogenetic VIP-interneuron sample sizes of 160 neurons/5 sessions/3 mice (control) and 110/4/3 (R6/2). The processing pipeline (Suite2p plus Cellpose for region-of-interest detection, DeepEthogram for behaviour labelling, ROIMatchGUI for tracking the same neuron across days) is described in Methods only; none of its outputs are downloadable.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified. The sole data link (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20750675) returns 404 from doi.org, the Zenodo API, both Zenodo HTML paths and DataCite; Zenodo search finds no such record. The statement 'Source data are provided with this paper' is not true in the files: the article page and PubMed Central both list only three supplementary objects — a 34.8 kB p-value table, the reporting summary and the peer review file — and probes for MOESM4-14 all 403. Everything else is 'available from the corresponding authors on reasonable request', which the rubric treats as an automatic failure.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not reachable, but fails on the paper's own description. Any usable label (genotype, disease stage, movement-modulated yes/no, light versus no-light trial) would have to be constructed by joining per-neuron fluorescence traces to behavioural video timestamps and to per-animal metadata across files that are not published.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs are per-neuron delta-F-over-F0 calcium traces and forelimb kinematic trajectories. Neither is downloadable; the only obtainable file contains p-values describing those inputs.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are clearly described in Methods (delta-F/F0, z-scored; imaging at 512x512 pixels, ~1 um per pixel; behaviour video at 60-100 Hz). This is the one Part A item the paper does well, but it is from the text, not from files.

a5_enough_rows.note: The only verified file has 187 rows of statistics. The biologically meaningful unit here is the mouse (8 control + 8 R6/2 in the main cohort, 3 + 3 in the optogenetics cohort), far under the ~400 needed even for classification; neuron counts of ~1,300 are pseudo-replicates nested within 16 animals.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 34.8 kB verified; the unpublished raw two-photon movies would be hundreds of gigabytes, the extracted traces likely a few hundred megabytes.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Moot. If the trace tables were ever released they would fit a laptop easily; the raw imaging stacks would not.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all, because no file contains the counts. Worse, the data availability statement claims source data are provided with the paper and they are not, so the paper's description already disagrees with the files.

a8_label_provenance.note: Mixed and partly circular. Behaviour-state labels come from DeepEthogram, a trained neural-network behaviour classifier, so they are another model's output; 'movement-modulated neuron' labels are computed from the same delta-F/F0 traces that would be the features, via a shuffle test — textbook leakage by construction. Genotype is a real, clean label, but there are only 16 animals carrying it.

existing_models.name: LSTM-encdec (long short-term memory encoder-decoder) for multi-limb decoding from two-photon calcium imaging, J. Neural Engineering 2024 / bioRxiv 2023.11.30.569459
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to decode continuous four-limb trajectories of running mice from one cortical hemisphere; exact metric and split not retrieved beyond the abstract. Training data deposited at Mendeley Data rk2xywhx7w.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The low sampling rate of two-photon imaging relative to limb movement, and the indirect relationship between calcium fluorescence and spiking.

existing_models.name: Attention-based CNN-BiLSTM (convolutional neural network plus bidirectional long short-term memory) multi-task decoder, arXiv 2504.16917
existing_models.score_and_split: 93.1% accuracy for contralateral binary forelimb classification and ~85% for multiclass, across datasets; split definition not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalising a decoder trained on one hemisphere/animal to bilateral and to new animals.

existing_models.name: RADICaL (deep learning framework for single-trial neural population dynamics from calcium imaging), Nature Neuroscience 2022
existing_models.score_and_split: Infers single-trial population dynamics at sub-frame temporal resolution from two-photon data; benchmark numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Recovering fast single-trial dynamics from slow, noisy calcium signals.

existing_models.name: DeepEthogram (supervised behaviour classification from raw video pixels), eLife 2021
existing_models.score_and_split: >90% single-frame accuracy on mouse and fly benchmark videos, matching expert human labellers; code at github.com/jbohnslav/deepethogram. This paper itself used it and reports per-class F1 scores in Extended Data.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Rare behaviours with few positive examples, and transfer across labs and camera setups.

backbone.name: None appropriate. Calcium-trace foundation models exist in research form (RADICaL, latent-dynamics models such as LFADS) but there is no open freeze-and-head backbone for per-neuron two-photon traces comparable to ESM-2 for proteins.
backbone.licence: Article text is Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (verified in the PubMed Central XML); the data it describes is not released at all, so no data licence applies.

integration.partner_dataset: Allen Institute Brain Observatory two-photon calcium imaging (tens of thousands of mouse cortical neurons with Cre-line identity) would be the obvious partner for a cell-type-from-activity model.
integration.join_key: Cre driver line / interneuron subtype label plus cortical layer depth — a categorical key, not a stable identifier.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a classifier trained to read interneuron subtype from spontaneous activity in healthy visual cortex still work in diseased motor cortex, and does its confidence drop track Huntington's disease progression? — unanswerable here, because this paper releases none of the traces needed on its side of the join.

controls.positive_control: Would have been strong if data existed: the paper's own headline effect (VIP-interneuron hypoactivity in R6/2 mice) is a known signal a working classifier must recover, and genotype is a hard, non-circular label.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling across animals (not across neurons, which would leak through within-animal correlation) is runnable in principle; not runnable in practice with no data.
controls.external_validation: The paper contains a genuine second cohort — the zQ175DN knock-in mouse model, a different Huntington's disease model imaged at a different site — which would have made an excellent held-out test. Its data is also unreleased.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is supportable: the only downloadable file is a 187-row table of p-values, so nothing can be modelled, and even with the traces the honest claim would be limited to 'distinguishes Huntington's-model from control motor cortex among 16 mice from two laboratories', which 16 animals cannot support against animal-level cross-validation.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-neuron calcium activity in motor cortex to predict whether a mouse carries the Huntington's disease mutation.
plain_idea.train_on: What the model would see per example: the time course of calcium fluorescence (a proxy for how much a neuron fired) for one neuron around a movement, plus its molecular subtype and cortical depth. The paper reports roughly 1,300 VIP-interneurons across 71 imaging sessions, but the independent unit is the animal: 16 mice. None of it is downloadable.
plain_idea.predict: Output would be the animal's genotype (Huntington's disease model versus littermate control) and, as a second task, disease stage. The true answer comes from mouse genotyping of the transgene, which is a real laboratory measurement and not model-derived.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: If activity alone flagged genotype before motor symptoms appeared, preclinical Huntington's groups would gain a cheap circuit-level readout for testing drugs. Even a failure would quantify how much animal-to-animal variability swamps the disease signal.

more_or_better_data.why: We have no data at all: the Zenodo deposit 404s and the only file is 34.8 kB of p-values. The existing decoders were trained on released datasets (e.g. Mendeley Data rk2xywhx7w).

confidence_score.why: Calibrated per-prediction confidence needs many animals per group; the paper has 8 versus 8 in the main cohort and 3 versus 3 in the optogenetics cohort, and none of those traces are public.

models_beatable.why: The movement decoders are 2022-2025 deep models with unclear held-out-animal splits, so an honest re-evaluation would be legitimate — but that project would use their data, not this paper's, so it is not an argument for this candidate.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition outright: our model cannot see everything the baseline sees, because we have no inputs. There is no join key and no evaluation split.

label_elsewhere.sources: Not scored — the verdict is reject. For completeness: mouse genotype labels paired with public two-photon calcium traces exist in the Allen Institute Brain Observatory and in the MICrONS and DANDI archives, but those are healthy-animal or different-disease cohorts, and I did not search them for Huntington's models.
label_elsewhere.join_key: Cre driver line / cell-type label (categorical, not a stable accession)
label_elsewhere.why: Public calcium-imaging atlases could supply cell-type labels for pretraining, but no public resource carries this paper's specific Huntington's-model-versus-control label, so there is no external validation set.

ml_idea: The idea considered and abandoned: train an animal-level classifier that reads Huntington's disease genotype and disease stage from per-neuron movement-aligned calcium traces in motor cortex, with leave-one-mouse-out cross-validation, the zQ175DN knock-in cohort as an independent external test, and the optogenetic stimulation arm as a causal check (does stimulation move R6/2 mice toward the control side of the decision boundary?). It is a genuinely good design and it is dead on arrival because the traces are not published.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no data exists to size. The one file obtained is 34.8 kB and opens in under a second.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Resolve the Zenodo digital object identifier in the data availability statement before anything else. It took one HTTP request and returned 404, which killed the project in under a minute.

verdict_reason: A1 fails, verified in the files. The only stated data location, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20750675, returns 404 from doi.org, the Zenodo API, both Zenodo HTML paths and DataCite, and no matching record turns up in Zenodo search. The claim 'source data are provided with this paper' does not hold: the Nature page and PubMed Central each list exactly three supplementary objects, and the only data-like one is a 34,840-byte spreadsheet of 187 statistical test results; probes for eleven further supplementary objects all returned 403. Everything usable is 'available from the corresponding authors on reasonable request'. Secondary failures confirm it: A5 (16 mice is the real sample size, not ~1,300 neurons) and A8 (behaviour labels come from DeepEthogram, a trained classifier, and 'movement-modulated' labels are computed from the very traces that would be the features). Worth re-checking in a few months if the Zenodo deposit goes live, but even then the animal-level sample size is too small.
